### Highlights

#### League RPC is an application now, not a terminal window
Version 3 was an exe you ran in a console and configured by typing flags after it.

- Every setting has a home on a settings screen. There are no command-line flags any more.
- Closing the window hides it to the system tray. Your presence keeps running until you quit from there.
- It can start with Windows, hidden, so it is already waiting when you sit down to play.
- Light and dark themes, and a first-run walkthrough that says plainly what the app does and does not do. It does not launch League for you.

#### It updates itself
Hearing about a new version used to mean spotting a line in the console and going to download an exe.

- New versions are fetched, checked against a signature, and staged in the background. Restarting to apply one is your call.
- A single Windows notification when a release is ready, plus a dot on the About tab. The notification can be turned off without turning off updates.
- The changelog for a staged version is readable inside the app before you commit to it.

#### You decide what your presence says
The text Discord showed was fixed. Now it is yours to edit.

- Separate templates for in client, champ select, in game, and spectating, each with a live preview as you type.
- Placeholders for champion, queue, rank, KDA, creep score and game time.

#### Rebuilt from scratch in Go
No Python, no runtime to install, one program.

- Lighter on memory and CPU while it sits in the tray waiting for League to open.
- Everything version 3 showed is still here: summoner icons, rank emblems, KDA and creep score, champion skins including the animated ultimates, TFT companions, Arena and spectating.
- Windows only. Vanguard ended Linux support, and there is no macOS build.

#### Installed, not unzipped
- Setup installs for your user alone. It never asks for administrator rights and never touches shared files.
- It uninstalls from Windows' own apps list like anything else.
